SR-001.justification: Synthetic blocks with a frame claiming 100000 octets and a first-frame offset past the end end the walk and skip the rest; a block with status 0 yields no cursor (a_block_still_owned_by_the_kernel_is_not_read). The ring path of the veth suite (8/8) reads real blocks through the same walker.

SR-002.justification: The doctest calls recv twice while the first Packet is alive and is required not to compile; cargo test --doc reports it compile-fail ok. The ring is released only at the next recv (src/sys/linux.rs ring_next).

SR-003.justification: Exhaustive over buffers up to 24 octets and every start/length: either the tag lands inside the buffer with the rest intact or the buffer is untouched; no panic. tests/veth.rs::only_the_chosen_ethertypes_arrive_tagged_or_not_each_with_a_timestamp asserts wire length equals captured length and the tag position on real frames, on both receive paths. A filter returning a 20-octet snap length yields data of 20 and a wire length of 60, flagged truncated, on the ring and the plain path.

SR-004.justification: A frame of another EtherType sent first is not delivered; src/bpf.rs::tests::the_builder_refuses_what_the_kernel_would rejects empty, oversized, out-of-range-jump, bad-scratch and no-return programs. The open sequence creates the socket with protocol 0 and attaches the filter before bind (src/sys/linux.rs open).

SR-005.justification: In a child process: after drop_capabilities, CapEff and CapPrm in /proc/thread-self/status are zero, the already open socket sends and receives, and a new open fails PermissionDenied naming CAP_NET_RAW. Passed on ring and plain paths.

SR-006.justification: F_GETFD on an open Linux socket has FD_CLOEXEC; the BSD backend opens /dev/bpf with O_CLOEXEC and sets FD_CLOEXEC on its membership socket (src/sys/bsd.rs open_device, join_groups) — reviewed, not run on BSD.

SR-007.justification: Config::new leaves both flags false; the backends enable them only from those flags.

SR-008.justification: 100000 frames sent in batches; received plus stats().dropped equals 100000 and stats().received equals the frames seen, on both receive paths. Sparse traffic is kept: 50 frames 3 ms apart all wait in the ring while the reader is busy (sparse_frames_wait_in_the_ring_while_the_reader_is_busy).

SR-009.justification: Scenario 1 passed (send_at without tx_time is InvalidInput, tests/veth.rs::launch_time_needs_configuration_and_a_qdisc_that_honours_it). Scenario 2 (etf drops a past launch time and tx_errors counts it) is implemented and tested, but the test skipped: the local Docker kernel has no sch_etf. It runs in the ubuntu-24.04 CI lane.
